title: Compute kernels and instancing
summary: Use compute kernels and instanced geometry to update and draw repeated objects on the GPU.

blocks.text: ComputeKernel receives a named ShaderResource map, WGSL source and optional workgroup size. dispatch returns a ComputeCommand; it does not automatically submit work to the device. Queue that command with Scene.addCompute so the frame pipeline can execute it.

The dispatch size counts workgroups, not particles. Guard out-of-range global invocation IDs in WGSL. Allocate buffer usages for every consumer: a storage buffer read by a shader and updated by the CPU also needs the relevant COPY_DST usage.

Instanced repeats one template’s compatible geometry using a per-instance storage buffer. Standard layout uses 12 floats per instance; extended layout uses 16 and permits non-uniform scale. Position, rotation, scale, color, visible count and offset are exposed through public setters and options. instanceData is CPU-side storage; updateInstances/dirty state controls upload.

Instanced.compute accepts source or a kernel and can automatically dispatch each frame. EnsureGPUBuffer/getInstanceGPUBuffer bridges the storage buffer to compute. Avoid uploading stale CPU instanceData after a compute shader writes the authoritative positions, or the upload can overwrite the simulation. Explicit readback is asynchronous and can stall if used in a per-frame CPU loop.

animateStaggered uses seconds in its own options, unlike AnimOptions.duration. Large instance counts also change the firstInstance packing mode and reduce the representable state-index range; see the memory guide.

Arrange builds common repeated layouts and provides CPU InstanceItem wrappers or GPU instancing. GPU mode shares one template and instance state; CPU mode can give each clone a different hierarchy or material. Pick based on the required behavior, then profile the intended count.
A small compute grid isolates resource binding and dispatch from the separate instancing example above.
